transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-03-29 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE); Maya Chen (Redwood SE); Elena Rossi (Citrine Head of IT); Derek Moore (Citrine Security Architect); Priya Shah (Citrine Compliance)

Auto-summary (auto-generated):
- Goal: Review SAML/SCIM setup and validate RBAC/least-privilege patterns for Citrine's pilot; confirm SOC2/ISO artifact needs, audit log retention, and KMS options.
- Agreed pilot scope: SAML SSO + SCIM provisioning + role-mapping test + audit log sample.
- Action items: share metadata, role diagrams, schedule pilot week of 2026-04-06.

Topics covered:
- SAML metadata exchange and identity provider (IdP) requirements
- SCIM attribute mapping and group sync cadence
- RBAC model (admin tiers, service accounts, least-privilege templates)
- Audit logs, retention, and redaction for SOC2/ISO artifacts
- Encryption options: BYOK / KMS / HSM and key rotation
- Data residency and private deployment constraints

Transcript body (timestamps approximate, transcription imperfect):
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone thanks for joining. Quick intros — I'm Jordan, AE on this account. Maya is our solutions engineer.
[00:06] Maya: hi, uh, hi all. I'll be covering a few of the technical bits — sam-el and skim, sorry SCIM and RBAC mapping.
[00:12] Elena: thanks. we're excited to get this scoped, we want to make sure the pilot covers our least privilege requirements.
[02:15] Derek: quick context, Citrine is based in the EU, primary region Frankfurt eu-central-1, we have strict residency and encryption rules — we need to KEEP logs inside EU for at least 2 years. Any export needs approval.
[03:10] Maya: Understood. Redwood supports region pinning for both hosted and private control planes, we can pin the data plane to eu-central, and audit logs can be configured to persist to your S3 in-region or pushed to your SIEM.
[04:01] Priya: For SOC 2 and ISO we will need redacted examples of access logs and proof of key management controls — we don't need full PII in the sample, but the audit team wants the event flows.
[04:22] Jordan: We'll share a SOC2 summary and redacted log samples. Note that some of the logs are token-level and include model metadata — we can redact payloads on the samples.
[05:10] Derek: How does Redwood handle BYOK? We can't have Redwood hold master keys for EU data.
[05:28] Maya: You can choose BYOK — we integrate with customer KMS (Cloud KMS, AWS KMS, or HSM). In the private deployment option you can control keys in your VPC and we support encrypt-at-rest with customer keys. There are some limitations on hosted where we require a delegated KMS policy but keys remain in your account.
[06:05] Elena: Are the logs also encrypted with the same keys?
[06:12] Maya: Yes, we can envelope-encrypt logs. Primary data at rest is encrypted with your CMK, and the audit logs can be stored in your S3 bucket with server-side encryption using your KMS key.
[07:00] Speaker 1 (auto): so for SAML — we have Okta as our IdP. We want automatic provisioning with groups mapped to roles.
[07:20] Jordan: Ok cool. Our recommended pattern is SCIM group-to-role mapping; admin tiers (org-admin, sec-admin, app-admin) and service accounts for integrations.
[08:10] Derek: We need to avoid excessive permissions for service accounts. Can we have scoped service credentials that only allow specific model routes?
[08:25] Maya: Yes, we provide token scoping; you can issue API keys scoped to model, route, and TTL. For Dedicated/private you can also assign quota and rate limits per key.
[09:05] Priya: On RBAC, we need an auditable mapping — who granted what and when. Do audit logs capture role changes and SCIM events?
[09:20] Maya: All provisioning events — SCIM create/update/delete, role-binding changes, SAML logins — are emitted to the audit stream. Each event includes actor, timestamp, and the object state change. Note transcription might miss some field names (e.g., K-V cache sounded like K-V cash).
[10:30] Elena: For our security review we also want least-privilege templates — like default developer role can't export embeddings or run bulk exports.
[10:45] Jordan: We have pre-baked templates and can share a least-privilege starter pack that the SE team customizes for you.
[12:00] Derek: SCIM specifics: we expect group sync every 15 minutes or on-demand. What are the throttling/SCIM rate limits?
[12:18] Maya: SCIM is rate limited on hosted tiers to protect the control plane — default is 1 request/sec with bursts; Dedicated can increase that. For the pilot we can provision a higher burst allowance. We'll document recommended backoff logic.
[13:35] Elena: We use nested groups heavily, will SCIM flatten or preserve nesting?
[13:44] Maya: Our SCIM implementation preserves groups and adds group-membership attributes; nested groups are flattened into resolved membership for role mapping, but we retain the parent-child relation in the audit logs.
[15:00] Jordan: timeline question — what's your pilot acceptance criteria and timeline?
[15:07] Elena: timeline: pilot in April, production by May if pilot goes well. Acceptance: 1) SAML login success for 10 test users, 2) SCIM provisioning of groups and role assignment works, 3) audit logs show provisioning and role changes, 4) data residency enforced to eu-central and logs retained 2 years.
[16:20] Derek: Also need encryption attestations and KMS integration steps in our checklist.
[17:05] Maya: we'll provide a runbook: steps to exchange SAML metadata, SCIM base URL and token, expected attributes (email, externalId, groups), and sample mapping JSON. We'll also share guidance on service accounts and API key scoping.
[18:40] Priya: On the audit side — can we get a streaming export to our SIEM? We use Splunk.
[18:50] Maya: Yes, we support syslog/HTTPS push to SIEM or S3 bucket export. For hosted we have an export bridge; for private you can stream directly within VPC.
[20:10] Derek: For SOC2 evidence, do you provide time-bound retention policies and retention proofs?
[20:30] Jordan: We'll supply policy configs and sample retention lifecycle rules. For proofs we can provide redacted log bundles and a signed manifest showing retention times.
[22:00] Elena: about least privilege, want a specific example — developer role: read-only access to model output, no export, cannot delete models, cannot change billing settings.
[22:18] Maya: Right, we can implement role entitlements at that granularity. Entitlements are implemented via role -> permission set -> resource scope.
[24:40] Derek: network controls — in private deployment can we restrict egress to specific S3 endpoints?
[24:50] Maya: Yes, in VPC-deployed private we support egress controls, and Dedicated has IP allow lists per customer.
[26:00] Elena: Who on Redwood will be our point for the pilot?
[26:05] Jordan: I'll own the commercial and coordination. Maya will run the technical pilot and be the SE lead.
[27:20] Priya: A small nit - do you support SCIM subset sync so we can only sync a handful of groups?
[27:35] Maya: Yes, you can restrict sync to specific group filters or supply a SCIM filter param on the endpoint.
[28:40] Jordan: Ok let's walk through the immediate deliverables — Jordan will send SAML metadata, Maya will send role maps.
[29:10] Speaker 2 (system): there was a brief audio glitch at 00:30 — apologies if anything missed.
[30:00] Derek: Could we get an SLA on authentication failures and a fallback if IdP is down?
[30:20] Maya: For SSO we support cached sessions and a fallback to emergency admin email OTP if your IdP is unavailable, but that requires enabling an emergency admin flow and is logged for audits. For strict security customers we recommend a Dedicated/private deployment with an SSO failover pattern.
[32:05] Elena: For the SOC2 audit, who signs off on the redaction? Our legal team will need to confirm.
[32:15] Jordan: We'll provide redacted bundles and a checklist for you/legal to validate.
[33:40] Priya: Can we get sample policy text for RBAC changes so we can include in our internal SOPs?
[33:50] Maya: Yes — we'll include policy snippets for role creation, approval workflow, and emergency access procedures.
[35:00] Derek: Any limitations on SCIM attribute types? We rely on employeeNumber and costCenter attributes.
[35:12] Maya: SCIM supports custom attributes; we accept extended schemas and will map those to metadata fields. We'll include the mapping template.
[36:20] Elena: For logs retention, can we archive older logs to Glacier-equivalent?
[36:30] Maya: Sure, we can configure lifecycle rules in your S3 to archive after X days; we recommend hot storage for 90 days then archive.
[37:40] Jordan: circling back to acceptance criteria — we'll capture these in a one-pager and share.
[38:50] Elena: One more — provisioning errors and reconcile processes — if SCIM fails for a batch, is there a retry mechanism?
[39:05] Maya: Yes, SCIM errors are queued and retried with an exponential backoff; failures emit an alert to the audit stream and to your configured pager.
[40:40] Derek: Also need to ensure service account tokens are rotated automatically.
[40:50] Maya: We support automatic rotation for service credentials and can set TTLs and rotation policies per account.
[42:15] Priya: Are role change approvals captured via workflow? We want an approval step for privileged role grants.
[42:30] Maya: We support an approval workflow integration with your ticketing system (e.g., Jira). Approvals are recorded in the audit log and can be required for certain role classes.
[44:00] Jordan: Alright great — let me summarize next steps and owners.
[44:05] Jordan: Action items: (1) I will send SAML metadata and SOC2 summary; (2) Maya will send SCIM mapping template and RBAC diagrams; (3) Derek will share residency list and CIDRs; (4) schedule pilot for week of Apr 6.
[45:00] Elena: That sounds good. We'll confirm internal stakeholders and provide test users.
[46:30] Jordan: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the packet and a calendar invite for pilot kickoff.
[47:40] Meeting closed.
